body:
Observed in one session, 2026-08-29, doing mutation testing with `cp` and `sed`:

1. A stale anchor left the mutant UNAPPLIED. pytest printed a green summary, which is
   indistinguishable from "the suite caught nothing". Caught only because a stray traceback
   happened to print.
2. `cp cps/admin.py /tmp/$(basename $f)` and `cp cps/api/admin.py /tmp/$(basename $f)` both wrote
   `/tmp/admin.py`. The restore put a 476-line SPA module on top of a 3,788-line one; the tree only
   failed at import.
3. A restore was assumed rather than verified, and a `git checkout --` on a file whose fix was
   uncommitted silently discarded that fix.

All three produce a plausible result. None of them announce themselves.

ADDRESSED by tests/mutation/mutate.py, which refuses to report a verdict it cannot stand behind:
the anchor must match exactly once or the run is an ERROR and not a verdict; backups are
path-derived so same-basename modules cannot collide; the restore is hash-verified against the
pre-mutation digest and a mismatch is loud; and a SURVIVING mutant exits non-zero, because a gap in
the suite is a finding rather than a pass. tests/unit/test_mutation_harness.py pins all four
behaviours.

Filed rather than closed silently because the finding is the failure mode, not the tool: anyone
mutating by hand still hits all three.
title: Mutation testing by hand has three failure modes that all report as a PASS
